question.text: What is the MAXIMUM investment a standard (non-LVF) Category III AIF can make in one investee company, directly or through units of other AIFs?

answer.text: 10% of investable funds (or NAV, as elected and disclosed in PPM)

explanation.text: The Logic: A standard (non-LVF) Category III AIF is limited to investing not more than 10% of its investable funds in a single investee company, directly or through units of other AIFs. The basis of calculation (Investable Funds or NAV) is as elected and disclosed in the PPM. The Trap: 5% and 15% are not prescribed thresholds. The 20% figure is the Large Value Fund (LVF) carve-out and does not apply to standard Cat III AIFs. Note: Confirm in the PPM whether concentration is computed on Investable Funds or NAV, since the disclosed basis governs how the 10% limit is measured.
